key_point: Gordon Freeman never speaks, so the player becomes him
title: In over 25 years of Half-Life, Gordon Freeman has never said a single word.
caption: In over 25 years of Half-Life, Gordon Freeman has never said a single word. #gamefacts #didyouknow #gaming #halflife #valve #gordonfreeman

Gordon Freeman has never said a single word in any Half-Life game.

Valve kept him silent on purpose, and cut the cutscenes too. The whole story plays out through his eyes, so the player becomes Gordon.

The other characters talk to him constantly, and even joke about it. In Half-Life 2, Alyx says: "Man of few words, aren't you?"

title: In Metal Gear Solid, Psycho Mantis reads your memory card and names the Konami games you'v
caption: In Metal Gear Solid, Psycho Mantis reads your memory card and names the Konami games you've played. #gamefacts #didyouknow #gaming #metalgearsolid #psychomantis #kojima

instagram.caption:
In Metal Gear Solid (1998), Psycho Mantis reads your PlayStation memory card and comments on the other Konami games you've saved.

He then asks you to put your controller on the floor and makes it move with his "psychic power", using the rumble.

He dodges every attack because he reads your inputs. The fix: plug your controller into port 2.

key_point: a stranger's small kindness on a snowy hill became Dark Souls' online system
title: Dark Souls' online messages were inspired by strangers pushing cars up a snowy hill.
caption: Dark Souls' online messages were inspired by strangers pushing cars up a snowy hill. #gamefacts #didyouknow #gaming #darksouls #fromsoftware #soulslike

instagram.caption:
Dark Souls director Hidetaka Miyazaki once got stuck on a snowy hill. Strangers got out and pushed the cars up, one by one, then drove away before anyone could thank them.

He never met them again, but he never forgot it.

That's where Dark Souls' online system came from: messages, bloodstains and summon signs left by players you'll never meet, helping you anyway.

key_point: The Sims was born after its creator lost his home in a fire and had to rebuild his life
title: The Sims exists because its creator lost his home in a fire.
caption: The Sims exists because its creator lost his home in a fire. #gamefacts #didyouknow #gaming #thesims #willwright #maxis

instagram.caption:
The Sims exists because its creator lost his home in a fire.

In 1991 the Oakland firestorm burned Will Wright's house down. He had to rebuild his life from nothing, and buying every chair and plate again made him wonder why we own what we own.

His own company called the idea a dollhouse game and didn't want it. It came out in 2000 and became the best-selling PC game of its time.

key_point: a Game Boy burned in a Gulf War bombing still turned on and played Tetris
title: This Game Boy was burned in a bombing during the Gulf War. It still works.
caption: This Game Boy was burned in a bombing during the Gulf War. It still works. #gamefacts #didyouknow #gaming #gameboy #nintendo #tetris

This Game Boy was burned in a bombing during the Gulf War. It still works.

Its owner, a US serviceman, mailed the melted console to Nintendo hoping it could be repaired. The technicians put a Tetris cartridge in and it turned on.

Nintendo sent him a new one and kept the burned Game Boy on display in its New York store for years, still running Tetris.

caption: Grand Theft Auto became what it is because of a bug in the police cars. #gamefacts #didyouknow #gaming #gta #grandtheftauto #rockstargames

Grand Theft Auto became what it is because of a bug in the police cars.

It began in the mid-90s as a racing game called Race'n'Chase, and it was close to being cancelled. Then a glitch made the police ram the player instead of following.

title: Atari's E.T. game sold so badly that the company buried it in the desert.
caption: Atari's E.T. game sold so badly that the company buried it in the desert. #gamefacts #didyouknow #gaming #atari #etgame #retrogaming

instagram.caption:
Atari's E.T. game sold so badly that the company buried it in the desert.

One programmer had five weeks to make it in time for Christmas 1982. Atari made millions of cartridges, and millions came back unsold.

In 1983 truckloads were dumped in a landfill in New Mexico. For 30 years people called it a myth. In 2014 a dig found the cartridges.

key_point: Silent Hill's famous fog was a trick to hide what the PlayStation could not draw
title: Silent Hill's fog was there to hide what the PlayStation couldn't draw.
caption: Silent Hill's fog was there to hide what the PlayStation couldn't draw. #gamefacts #didyouknow #gaming #silenthill #konami #survivalhorror

instagram.caption:
Silent Hill's fog was there to hide what the PlayStation couldn't draw.

In 1999 the console could only show a short distance in 3D. Instead of letting buildings pop in, the team covered the whole town in fog and darkness.

Not seeing what's ahead made the game far scarier. The fog became the series' trademark and stayed long after it was needed.

key_point: Sony built the PlayStation after Nintendo publicly walked away from their joint console
title: The PlayStation exists because Nintendo betrayed Sony in public.
caption: The PlayStation exists because Nintendo betrayed Sony in public. #gamefacts #didyouknow #gaming #playstation #sony #nintendo

instagram.caption:
The PlayStation exists because Nintendo betrayed Sony in public.

In 1991 Sony announced a CD add-on for the Super Nintendo at a big trade show. The next day, Nintendo said it would work with Philips instead.

Sony's boss was furious and told his team to build their own console. The PlayStation came out in 1994 and outsold the Nintendo 64 three to one.

instagram.caption:
The Legend of Zelda was the first NES game that let you save.

Before it, long games made you write down passwords on paper. Zelda's gold cartridge had a small battery inside that kept your progress when the console was off.

Some of those batteries still hold a save almost 40 years later.
